entries.text: A property is listed only when every active step has it and composition preserves it on the natural domain. Compositions of analytic, entire, rational, polynomial, Möbius, injective and proper (into ℂ) maps keep that property.
Each step is judged on its own natural domain, off its branch cut. So log is injective but exp is not; z ↦ 1/z is Möbius but not proper into ℂ, since |1/z| stays bounded as z → ∞.
The list is sound but not complete. For example, exp followed by log returns z, yet neither step is rational, so "rational" is not claimed.

Custom formulas are classified from their expression tree: only z, constants, +, −, ×, ÷ and integer powers count as rational. A polynomial formula has its exact degree found numerically before "proper" is claimed.

entries.text: The switch in the middle of the top bar picks the view ({x} {x} {x}). X → Y shows the two planes side by side: the shapes on the left, their images on the right, each pane with its own Plane · Sphere switch ({x} {x} for the left pane, {x} {x} for the right). The right plane has a derivative gauge under the probe. Phase is one wide panel that colours each point of X by arg F, with modulus contours, on the plane or on the Riemann sphere; the shapes are outlined. Landscape is one wide panel that lifts |F| over X into a surface, in the phase colours or in plaster: zeros are pits, poles are peaks; for a map with a branch cut, All sheets draws its whole Riemann surface instead of the cut principal branch (best with height Re F or Im F). Each view keeps its own camera and plane view. Sphere places a pane on the Riemann sphere, with ∞ at the north pole. You draw on it as in the plane (shapes on the left, targets on the right; Annulus, Sector and Polar grid draw in Plane only): a Disc or Circle is a cap of the sphere, and one whose rim passes ∞ becomes a half-plane or a line. With Select, drag a shape to move it (over ∞ it changes kind) and empty space to turn the globe; in every tool the middle button, Space held or two fingers turn it. The Phase key check in the right plane's options of X → Y paints the portrait's colours under it, so a colour of the portrait reads off as a value of w.

entries.text: Deformation in the top bar ({x}) plays the homotopy from z to F(z), step by step, in every view. In X → Y the two panes merge into one plane (one globe when the right pane shows its Sphere): X in grey, the moving image Ht(X), and the paths t ↦ Ht(z) of well-spread points. In Phase and Landscape it paints Ht. Each step deforms along its natural path: Ht is analytic for every t, starts at the identity and ends at the map. Möbius maps move along their one-parameter groups, powers along z1+(n−1)t; exp, sin, cos, tan, the hyperbolic functions, their inverses and rational maps are zoomed into, so their zeros, poles and cuts fly in from infinity (sin(tz)/t); a polynomial switches its zeros on one by one; Joukowski closes the unit circle onto [−1, 1]. A formula that is none of these, or a constant, moves along the straight line. The transport under the panel scrubs t and sets the speed and, for two or more steps, the order: one after another (0 ≤ t ≤ m) or all at once (0 ≤ t ≤ 1, every step at the same t). Paths ({x}) shows or hides the paths. Turning the deformation off splits the panes again and returns to t at the end. A focused step deforms that step only.
